ClassificationStoreConfigurationKeyGroup.description:
Every property but the pair is optional: one absent from the payload leaves the stored value
untouched, and a supplied one replaces it rather than merging into it. The three per assignment
ones are optional in both directions, so one carrying an explicit null clears it; `sorter` and
`mandatory` cannot be cleared and refuse an explicit null.

All five defaults therefore stand for "the payload did not carry it" rather than for a value,
which is why they are typed `mixed` - the two states have to stay distinguishable, and the
payload mapping substitutes the default for a missing key. `sorter` and `mandatory` used to
default to `0` and `false`, which made a payload naming neither reset them on an already stored
assignment; only a new assignment takes those values now, and it takes them from the repository.

Re-enabling restores the key configuration. This endpoint neither deletes nor re-creates any group assignment —

Note: disabling a key removes its group assignments, so a restored key belongs to no group, and its sorter,
mandatory flags and per-assignment overrides are gone. This endpoint creates no assignment and nothing else restores

get.description:
Download the configuration of one classification store as a single JSON file: the store, its sub groups,
collections, groups and keys, and the collection-group and key-group assignments between them.
Every entry is named by its identifier, so the file can be applied to another installation.
Refused with 409 while the store, or any collection, group, sub group or key in it, carries no identifier.

200.description: The store configuration as a JSON download

422 - Unprocessable Content

post.description: Apply a store configuration file to the store given in the URL, as a multipart file field. A file describing the store in the URL is restored into it: entries are matched by identifier, falling back to the name for a row that carries no identifier yet. An entry whose identifier the store does not carry is created, an entry whose name the store holds under another identifier is skipped and named in the report, and nothing is deleted - what the store carries and the file does not is left in place and named too. A file describing another store is imported as a duplicate instead: every sub group, collection, group and key gets a freshly generated identifier, the store keeps its own identifier and name, and the configuration the store held is removed and replaced by the file's. Importing the same file again gives the same store rather than a second copy. The report says which of the two happened and names what was removed. A replace also deletes data: removing a group removes every stored Classification Store value under it, on both storage engines, through the cascade of the value tables, and importing the file again does not bring those values back. storedValuesRemoved says so - it is a statement about the import, not a count of the values. Send dryRun to get the same report without writing anything, which is how a replace can be shown before it happens. Refused with 409 when the configuration cannot be applied - including a key whose field type is withdrawn as a key type, or wraps one no key is defined with, or cannot be held by the storage engine of the store - and with 422 when the file is not a parseable artifact.

file.description: Store configuration artifact as written by the export endpoint

dryRun.description: Report what would be decided - what a replace would remove included - and write nothing

200.description: Report of what the import created, updated, adopted, skipped, removed and left in place
